title: THE NEAREST
author: Ensemble
kind: étude (not a cycle work), made for the Studio's plea while the house chooses its programme
medium: A field of 629 dots in the browser (canvas, Web Audio): one dot per work of the Atlas of Data Art, ordered by year from left to right. Choosing one of the dossier's twelve candidate questions lights, in year order and optionally with one click per work, the works whose title or decisive move name its ground; hits read by hand and refused stay as hollow rings with their reason; each dot opens its work. Under the field: the candidate's named datasets as the Field's study 64 probed them.
embodies: How crowded the Atlas already stands on each candidate's ground, and whether the data a form would rest on can be fetched. Of 629 works: 1 Living past 1.5°C 24 · 2 Tipping points 3 (all on coral) · 3 The sixth extinction 9 · 4 Feeding everyone 6 · 5 Antibiotics 1 · 6 War between states 29 · 7 Nuclear weapons 0 · 8 Autocratic majority 3 · 9 Shared knowledge 21 · 10 Who controls advanced AI 104 (not read by hand) · 11 Wealth 1 · 12 Debt and poverty 0; 454 touch none of the twelve; 17 keyword hits refused by hand. Grounds the Studio's Plea: 2 and Objection: 10.

atlas_neighbours: No Atlas work is mapped onto the Atlas itself here; the nearest in move are the works that make a corpus's own coverage visible, e.g. 'Have I Been Trained?' (a search over LAION-5B that shows an artist whether their work is already inside). Daylight: this étude asks not whether a work is in a corpus but where a new one would stand among the corpus's existing sentences, and it lays the whole corpus out each time.
